page: Microsoft Azure D4ds_v4 is a general-purpose virtual machine built on the x86_64 architecture. Hosted on Microsoft Hyper-V, the instance features an Intel Xeon Platinum 8272CL processor running at a base clock speed of 2.6 GHz. The hardware configuration provides 4 dedicated vCPUs spanning 2 physical cores with hyperthreading enabled (2 threads per core). Cache resources include 32 KB of L1 data cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and a shared 35 MB L3 cache. It incorporates instruction set extensions such as AVX-512 (including AVX512F and AVX512_VNNI) alongside AES cryptographic instructions.

The instance is provisioned with 16.0 GB of system memory, matching a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio at 4.0 GB per vCPU. Storage capabilities include a bundled 161 GB local SSD designed for temporary scratch storage or local caching, complementing Azure Premium Storage attachment capabilities. The configuration includes no discrete GPU hardware and allocates zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark results demonstrate modest computational throughput, consistent with a low-core older generation Xeon configuration. Single-threaded operations such as Geekbench single-core (1201.0) and gzip compression (24.28 GB/sec) score within average industry percentiles. Multi-core scaling remains constrained due to the 2 physical core baseline, with stress-ng multi-core (3678.27) and PassMark CPU score (4387.87) falling into lower tiers. Memory bandwidth records 27.12 GB/sec for uncached reads and 21.12 GB/sec for writes.

Given its balanced memory density and bundled local high-speed SSD, the D4ds_v4 provides cost-effective utility for light-to-moderate enterprise tasks. It is technically suited for low-traffic web applications, small microservices, CI/CD build agents, staging environments, and basic caching servers that do not require intensive parallel CPU computing.

The system features AVX-512 extensions and 35 MB of L3 cache, with no discrete GPU acceleration.
